synopsis: Chapter 8 and the glossary describe MSHA Table M-1 as a kinematic stopping-performance rule based on constant deceleration of 9.66 ft/s², approximately 2.94 m/s² or 0.3 g [f5890, f13634, f6425]. Its stopping-distance formulation uses d = v²/(2a), and the assumed deceleration is close to the worked example’s 3.0 m/s² level-ground value [f13645, f13650]. Chapter 8 gives system-response allowances of 0.5–2.5 seconds by weight class, plus one second of operator time; the glossary gives a two-second total delay for very heavy equipment, contributing 8.3 metres at 15 km/h, without explaining how that total maps to the weight-class allowances [f6058, f13658]. The corpus also describes prescribed stopping tests as running from brake-control actuation to standstill, including system response but excluding operator reaction, so planners should distinguish that test boundary from the operator-inclusive delay allowance [f6540, f6058].
